biography.plain_text: Helmut Horten (1909–1987) built one of West Germany's largest department-store groups. Its beginnings included stores acquired from Jewish owners under Nazi persecution, an advantage that shaped his early expansion. He later rebuilt and enlarged the chain before selling his shares and moving to Switzerland. His wife Heidi inherited the fortune derived from the business.

long_biography.plain_text:
Helmut Horten learned retailing as an apprentice at a Düsseldorf department store. In 1936 a Duisburg banker helped him establish a company that took over the Alsberg store from Jewish owners under Nazi persecution. Other such acquisitions followed. These transactions gave him an early platform, although much of the chain's later scale came from postwar rebuilding and further purchases.

Horten rebuilt his Duisburg operation and acquired the Merkur and DeFaKa chains, bringing dozens of stores under his control. He broadened their merchandise and grouped the businesses under his own name. After selling his company shares, he settled in Switzerland and established a foundation for medical research. He died there in 1987.
